title: Launcher console encoding: 3-mode policy for interactive + piped + UTF-8 terminals
desc: Bootstrap PowerShell, cmd.exe, and Git Bash to start in UTF-8 on Windows. Use when console output or argv is misread because shells still start in CP949/ANSI mode.
steps: Write UTF-8 bootstrap lines into both PowerShell profile files: set Console.InputEncoding, Console.OutputEncoding, and $global:OutputEncoding to UTF-8; set LANG=C.UTF-8, LC_ALL=C.UTF-8, PYTHONUTF8=1, and PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8; run chcp 65001.

Write Git Bash locale defaults into ~/.bashrc and source them from ~/.bash_profile: export LANG=C.UTF-8; export LC_ALL=C.UTF-8; export PYTHONUTF8=1; export PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8; export LESSCHARSET=utf-8.
Persist PYTHONUTF8=1 and PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 as user environment variables so every new Python process inherits UTF-8 even outside the shell bootstrap.
Verify fresh shells with cmd /c chcp, PowerShell console encodings, Git Bash LANG/LC_ALL/PYTHONUTF8/PYTHONIOENCODING, and python -c checks before blaming file contents.
If Bash argv is still mangled, use TryRecoverUtf8Argv or ASCII-only wrappers instead of guessing that the file is broken.
Keep tools/bootstrap_utf8_shells.ps1 only as the mechanical equivalent of the same steps.

SEE ALSO (reflex back-link 2026-06-11): ps-script-mojibake-is-output-encoding-first-not-argv -- if a .ps1 prints garbled Korean or U+FFFD, suspect the console OUTPUT encoding FIRST (set OutputEncoding=UTF8 at script start) before blaming the bash-to-powershell argv boundary; [Console]::InputEncoding does NOT touch -File positional argv.
author: claude
